newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slightly higher in dull market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slightly higher in dull market.

text.p: Argentine bonds, settling down after their breakneck pace earlier in the week, were virtually untraded in anticipation of the closure of the U.S. Treasuries market early Friday and Monday.
"The truth is that the market is very boring right now but it is sustained," said a trader at a local bank.
The FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 88-7/8. No trades in the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 were recorded on screens. It slipped $0.25 to 125.05 on Thursday.
Another trader said "there is no real news today."

Players predicted activity would be subdued through the session with the focus in the coming week set to turn to the anticipated launch of Argentina's $2.0 billion global issue split between a five- and a 20-year bond.
